answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Easy running can start now, which is what the first few days of the plan show. Keep every run short, flat and under a heart rate of 135, and stop if pain sharpens or moves to a new spot. Most runners need about two weeks of easy running before any faster work, so the next real decision comes in about two weeks.

A 10K five weeks after a marathon is possible, but only as a controlled effort, not a time goal. If your legs feel close to normal in about two weeks, we can add a few short faster runs. If they still feel heavy, run it easy or skip it.

Tell me what you want next: the 10K, or a spring marathon. Your answer sets the training block that follows these two easy weeks.

new.analysis:
## The week
The week went to plan. Each run hit its planned distance, the Wed Oct 14 workout ran two miles at marathon pace in four half-mile reps, and the rest days were rest. Nothing was overrun, so the load was as intended going into race day.

## The race
The race is where the goal slipped. The front half was on target, and the back half slowed noticeably.

| Stretch | Pace per mile |
| --- | --- |
| Front half | 8:32 |
| Back half | 8:58 |
| Whole race | 8:48 |

Sub-3:45 needs about 8:35 per mile over 26.2 miles, so the back half was the gap. Heart rate drift was modest at 6.5 beats, which points to muscle fatigue rather than a fitness limit. The course also climbed about 617 feet, which adds load to the quads over that distance, and the quads are what gave out.

## Load and recovery
The week's load score of 472 comes from the race itself, so the overload note is expected rather than a warning. Recovery means far less volume than last week's 41 miles and easy effort on every run. The heart rate ceiling of 135 sits just under your usual easy average of about 139, so the runs stay truly easy.

## Body check
Sore quads and calves and the left big toe blister are common after 26 miles, but both need watching day to day. Neither changes the plan yet. If either gets worse, stop running and get it checked.

## Next two weeks
Week two can rise toward about 15 miles, still all easy, if the legs feel close to normal. The choice between the 10K and the next goal comes after that, based on your answer.

safetyCallouts.title: Calf and leg soreness needs a check if it grows.
safetyCallouts.body: Sore quads and calves are common two days after a marathon, but stop running and see a doctor or physio if a calf gets more painful, swollen or warm, or if the pain spreads.

safetyCallouts.title: Watch the left big toe blister.
safetyCallouts.body: Keep it clean and covered during the easy runs. If it turns red, hot or swollen, or starts to drain, see a qualified health professional before the next run.
